header.userPrompt:
Make PRs opened by Orca flows always carry a GitHub closing keyword ("Closes #N" / "Closes owner/repo#N") in the PR description when the work closes or fixes a GitHub issue.

Current state:
- flows/issue-pr.sc and flows/issue-pr-bugfix.sc already append "Closes <shortRef>" explicitly — keep that.
- flows/simple.sc, implement.sc, implement-enhanced.sc and implement-interactive.sc call openPrIfGitHub without `context`, so the PR summariser (flow/src/main/scala/orca/pr/summarisePr.scala, prompt in flow/src/main/resources/orca/pr/prompts/summarise.md) never sees the user prompt. When the prompt says e.g. "fix #190" or links an issue URL, the PR body lacks "Closes #190" and GitHub does not link/close the issue.

Required:
1. The summariser must see the originating user prompt in the generic flows (pass it as context, or make openPrIfGitHub default to it — pick the simplest design that covers all built-in flows).
2. Update summarise.md so that when the context references a GitHub issue the branch closes or fixes, the body ends with a line "Closes #N" (or "Closes owner/repo#N" for another repo), one per issue; never invent issue numbers, and don't add it for issues only mentioned in passing.
3. Don't produce a duplicate "Closes" line in issue-pr.sc / issue-pr-bugfix.sc, which already append one deterministically.
4. Add/adjust tests where there is a deterministic seam (e.g. context reaching the summariser prompt). Update docs (README / flow scaladoc) only if they describe this behaviour.
